heading: About
body: I own architecture and performance on large codebases, and run the code review that keeps them maintainable. Most of what I build is infrastructure other people build on - low-code platforms, back-office systems, document management, e-commerce. React, Next.js and TypeScript on the front, Node.js and PostgreSQL behind it, with LLM features in the recent products. Most of it contract work, straight with the client rather than through a delivery layer.

achievements.language: Designed the DSL behind a low-code reporting platform - parser, editor and evaluation - so analysts could write their own formulas instead of filing tickets.
achievements.clients: Worked directly with clients in the EU and the US, with no manager in between - agreeing what should be built, then building it end to end.
achievements.platform: Owned the frontend architecture of that platform: a widget system where every table, chart and text block is configured at runtime, over customer databases.
achievements.payments: Built payments and subscriptions end to end - store receipt verification, webhooks, background jobs for renewal and expiry. The part that has to be right the first time.
achievements.ai: Took LLM features from prototype to production: retrieval, streaming responses and tool calling inside real product flows, not a demo chat.
achievements.performance: Kept large codebases fast after they had grown past the point where one person could hold them in their head.
achievements.review: Established the code review process the team kept running, and mentored the developers who joined after.

personal: I have worked with German, American, Israeli and Ukrainian teams, and most of my career has been remote, across timezones, with colleagues I have only ever met on a call. The same sentence carries different weight depending on who says it - direct feedback that is ordinary in one team reads as rudeness in another. Erin Meyer's The Culture Map is good on this. Knowing it removes a lot of friction that has nothing to do with the work.

I play the Dark Souls series. It teaches you to understand rather than to push harder: you get through a difficult place once you know how it works. Bugs are the same - guessing rarely gets you there, careful reading does.
I read manga, walk a lot, and make tea. Tea, incidentally, is the only skill on my LinkedIn that was endorsed without me asking.
